newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says U.S. envoy to take up his post May 9.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says U.S. envoy to take up his post May 9.

text.p: Vietnam said on Wednesday that Washington's first ambassador to Hanoi, former prisoner of war Douglas "Pete" Peterson, would take up his post on May 9.
The Communist Party's Nhan Dan newspaper said Peterson would be formally inaugurated in his role in Washington on April 29 and arrive in Hanoi at the end of the following week.

It quoted Peterson as saying in an interview with the official Vietnam News Agency that he aimed to contribute to healing the wounds from the war era and build a bridge linking the people of the two countries.
Peterson, a former fighter pilot, was captured in 1966 after being shot down on a mission near Vietnam's northern port town of Haiphong. He was held prisoner for 6-1/2 years.
His selection as the first postwar U.S. ambassador to Vietnam was confirmed by the Senate last week, following lengthy delays because of legal and political sensitivities surrounding the post.

Hanoi's own envoy-designate to Washington, Le Van Bang, was quoted separately by the daily Vietnam News as saying that one of his prime tasks would be to accelerate the normalisation of economic relations between the former foes.

Bang, who is due to take up his post at about the same time as his U.S. counterpart, said he would use his role to raise the American public's awareness of Vietnam as an independent and developing country and overcome the so-called "Vietnam Syndrome".
That term is used by Hanoi to mean a perceived tendency among both Americans and Vietnamese to view each other with mistrust as former enemies.
Vietnam is due to mark the 22nd anniversary of the fall of Saigon, the event which ended the Vietnam War, on April 30.
